mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points triggers risk-off sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal broad economic deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both INDPRO and RSAFS decline (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a monthly CPIAUCSL increase above 0.2% triggers equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances during late-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force (PAYEMS) indicates strong economic activity and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is rising (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 1200 thousand units signal weak consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with a federal funds rate above 1.5% signals economic distress and tight monetary policy, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises and FEDFUNDS > 1.5% (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In strong demand expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply chain disruptions and weak manufacturing, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances during strong demand expansions (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).
